title: Run record
description: A machine-checkable record of one executed evidence run. It ties a claim's evidence to a concrete command, commit, exit code and output log, so re-dating the ledger or citing a test that never ran fails the linter. An `anchor` is required: an SSH signature over the record's canonical bytes (see tools/anchor_subject.py) that L2 verifies against the committed allowed_signers, so an edit after signing stops verifying. It still does not prove the run was not fabricated: the key holder can re-sign, and replacing allowed_signers with a new signer bypasses the check (C-13).

runner.description: Test runner or tool that produced the output, e.g. 'cargo test', 'pytest', 'python3 setup/test_fstek.py'.

command.description: Exact command that was executed, including flags.

commit.description: Commit the run executed at. Must equal the evidence commit.

exit_code.description: Process exit code. A non-zero code cannot support a non-open status.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-11-07T12:00:00+03:00.

finished_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Its local date must equal the evidence date.

log.description: Path to the captured output, relative to the project root (or a URL, in which case the hash is not checked).

log_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the log bytes. Lint check L2 verifies it.

artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the evidence artifact at run time. Required when the evidence names a local artifact; L2 verifies it.

tests_run.description: Number of tests executed (not ignored, not filtered out).

tests_passed.description: Number of executed tests that passed. Must equal tests_run for a passing run.

anchor.description: An SSH signature over the canonical bytes of the run record (runner, command, commit, exit code, timestamps, log and optional artifact hashes, test counts; see tools/anchor_subject.py). The signed subject, its signature and the allowed_signers file are committed and hashed here. L2 recomputes the bytes and verifies the signature, so a record edited after signing stops verifying. The private key is not in the repository. The anchor does not stop the key holder, or anyone who can replace allowed_signers and re-sign: that is the remaining C-13 gap.

type.description: Signature scheme. Only ssh-ed25519 is implemented.

signer.description: Identity passed to `ssh-keygen -Y verify -I`; must appear in allowed_signers.

namespace.description: Signature namespace (`ssh-keygen -Y sign -n`). Pinned per channel: a static-analysis or sanitizer signature does not verify here.

subject.description: Path to the signed canonical subject, relative to --run-log-root.

subject_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the subject bytes. L2 verifies it.

signature.description: Path to the detached SSH signature (`ssh-keygen -Y sign` output).

signature_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the signature file. L2 verifies it.

allowed_signers.description: Path to the committed allowed_signers file used for verification.

date.description: Date the signature was made. For a backfilled record this is later than the run's finished_at: the signature proves immutability after signing, not the run date.
